subject: humanities
passage: In the early 1600s, plays at the Globe, an open-air playhouse in London, were performed in the afternoon and relied on daylight. There was no way to dim the light or darken the stage, and scenery was minimal. Yet many plays of the period include scenes set at night or during storms. Scholars note that in such scenes, characters often remark on the darkness, carry torches or lanterns, or describe the weather around them. These details suggest that playwrights ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: avoided writing night scenes because the stage could not show them.
choices.B: preferred indoor theaters, where candles let them control the light.
choices.C: used speech and props to suggest what the stage could not show.
choices.D: expected audiences to attend performances only after sunset.

explanation.why: The daylit Globe stage could not look dark or stormy, yet plays included night and storm scenes. Characters' remarks about darkness and weather, along with torches and lanterns, told the audience what the stage itself could not show.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says many plays of the period include night scenes, so playwrights did not avoid them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never mentions indoor theaters or candles, so it does not support a claim about playwrights' preferences.
explanation.C: Correct. Spoken descriptions and props like torches let the audience imagine darkness and storms in daylight.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says plays at the Globe were performed in the afternoon.
